newsitem.title: EGYPT: Qatar tells Israel no trade office without peace.
newsitem.headline: Qatar tells Israel no trade office without peace.

text.p: Qatar told Israel on Tuesday it would not proceed with the planned opening of a trade mission in the Jewish state unless there was progress in peace talks with the Palestinians.

"I met (Israeli Foreign Minister) David Levy half an hour ago and told him that unless there is progress on the Palestinian peace track we will not take action on our trade representation," Qatari Foreign Affairs Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani told a news conference in Cairo.
"We have frozen any developments in the normalisation of our relations with Israel," he added, reiterating the Gulf state's policy.
Hamad was speaking on the sidelines of the Middle East and North Africa Economic Conference aimed at integrating the region's economies.

Qatar and Oman have gone further than their Gulf Arab allies to establish economic ties with Israel but stopped short of full diplomatic relations pending the resolution off all Arab-Israeli conflicts.
The Jewish state has trade missions in the two countries, and Oman has opened a trade representation office in Tel Aviv. But Qatar has postponed opening a similar office in Israel.
Israel's right-wing government, which took office in June, has angered Arabs by rejecting the policy of land-for-peace that has underpinned Middle East peace efforts.
Talks with the Palestinians are snagged on a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment from the occupied West Bank town of Hebron that Israel was to have implemented early this year.
